Spectacular Bridge Crossings for Motorcyclists

Bridges are transitions — from one landscape to another, from mainland to island, from one chapter of your tour to the next. Some of Britain's bridges are engineering marvels that deserve to be ridden slowly and appreciated. Here are the crossings that make the journey part of the destination.

Iconic Crossings

  • Forth Road Bridge, Edinburgh: The crossing of the Firth of Forth with views to the iconic Victorian rail bridge alongside. Free for motorcycles since the Queensferry Crossing opened.
  • Skye Bridge: Connecting Kyle of Lochalsh to Skye. Free since 2004 and the gateway to one of Scotland's most magical islands. The views across to the Cuillins as you cross are spectacular.
  • Humber Bridge: Once the world's longest single-span suspension bridge. The 2.2km crossing gives enormous views across the Humber estuary. Free for motorcycles.
  • Menai Suspension Bridge, Anglesey: Thomas Telford's masterpiece linking mainland Wales to Anglesey. Built in 1826, it's still stunning. The views up and down the Menai Strait are beautiful.
  • Severn Bridge: The original M48 crossing into Wales. More dramatic than the newer Second Severn Crossing, with views across the Bristol Channel. Eastbound toll-free.

Hidden Gem Crossings

  • Kylesku Bridge, Sutherland: A graceful curved bridge across Loch a' Chairn Bhain on the NC500. The setting — mountains, lochs, and wilderness — makes this one of the most beautiful bridges in Britain.
  • Conwy Suspension Bridge: A Telford suspension bridge next to Conwy Castle. Ride the modern road bridge and walk back across the historic one.
  • Ballachulish Bridge, Glencoe: Spanning the narrows of Loch Leven with Glencoe's mountains as a backdrop.
  • Devil's Bridge, Kirkby Lonsdale: A medieval stone bridge over the River Lune. Not rideable (it's pedestrianised) but the view from it was described by Ruskin as one of the loveliest in England.

Causeways

  • Holy Island Causeway, Northumberland: A tidal causeway connecting the mainland to Lindisfarne. Passable only at low tide. Check tide tables carefully — getting caught by the tide is both dangerous and embarrassing. The experience of riding across a sea-level causeway with water on both sides is unique.
  • Eriskay Causeway, Outer Hebrides: Connecting Eriskay to South Uist. A modern causeway through the sea with views to Barra and the Atlantic.
Bridges are exposed to crosswinds. Large suspension bridges like the Humber and Forth can have significant wind effects, especially on motorcycles. Check weather conditions and be prepared for sudden gusts as you ride into exposed sections. Grip the tank with your knees and keep a relaxed but firm hold on the bars.

Bridge Photography Tips

  • Pull over before the bridge for a long-range shot showing the whole structure
  • Stop at viewpoints on the bridge itself (where safe and legal) for perspective shots
  • Golden hour light picks out bridge details beautifully
  • Include your motorcycle in the frame for scale and context

Every bridge tells a story of engineering ambition and human connection. Riding across Britain's great bridges is riding across history itself. Kylesku Bridge on the NC500 and Menai Suspension Bridge are the most beautiful crossings in Britain.
The Holy Island causeway to Lindisfarne is passable only at low tide, so check tide tables carefully.

faq.q: Which bridges are free for motorcycles?
faq.a: Several major crossings carry no toll for motorcycles. The Skye Bridge has been free since 2004, the Forth Road Bridge is free since the Queensferry Crossing opened, and the Humber Bridge is free for bikes. The Severn Bridge is toll-free eastbound. Always check current arrangements before relying on it, as tolling policies on UK crossings do change over time.

faq.q: How do I handle crosswinds on big suspension bridges?
faq.a: Large spans like the Humber and Forth can generate strong, gusty crosswinds, especially as you emerge from shelter onto the open deck. Check the weather beforehand, reduce speed, grip the tank firmly with your knees, and keep a relaxed but positive hold on the bars. Anticipate a sudden push as you pass towers or gaps and correct smoothly rather than snatching.

faq.q: How do I safely ride the Holy Island causeway?
faq.a: The causeway to Lindisfarne floods at high tide, so consult the published safe crossing times and never chance it as the tide turns. Vehicles are caught and swept every year, which is both dangerous and expensive. Ride across only within the stated window, watch for wet, slippery patches and sand on the tarmac, and allow time to enjoy the island before the tide closes the road again.

faq.q: Which is the most photogenic bridge to ride?
faq.a: Kylesku Bridge in Sutherland is a favourite: a graceful curved span across Loch a' Chairn Bhain, framed by mountains and wilderness on the NC500. The Menai Suspension Bridge, Telford's 1826 masterpiece, is another. For the best shots, pull over safely before the bridge for a full-structure image and place your motorcycle in the frame for scale and story.
